figures.caption: The GALE-CAST website's binary scorecard (validation_cm3.json), reproduced case by case: 24 hits, 4 misses, 9 false alarms, 3,386 correct negatives. Accuracy is dominated by correct negatives; the all-negative forecast scores 99.18%.
The same 3,423 cases split by primary station. Because X1 averages the three stations, a warning is issued for all three stations on the same date; station results are therefore not independent.

Precision, recall and F1 with 95% intervals. On both cohorts W1+X1 beats both event baselines on F1 (established). The level depends on the input construction: 24/28 hits with the website's procedure, fewer with training-consistent inputs.
The PF-C comparison for each primary station. With 8-10 events per station the intervals are wide.
Curves traced from the 3,423 saved W1 scores (not reconstructed from a confusion matrix), with the historical 0.601 point marked.
Next-day wind accuracy for the neural model and both reference forecasts on identical station-dates. MAE and RMSE are reported separately.

The website's wind MAE 0.5365 / RMSE 0.7723 / MASE 0.6782 are reproduced exactly only after two post-processing steps fitted on the evaluation period itself. W1's own wind output has MAE 0.987; issue-day persistence on the same cases has MAE 0.474.
Each output has its own unit and panel. Compare model and reference forecasts within a panel. Read MAE together with RMSE and signed bias in the source table.

Binned counts replace a scatter so that no individual station-day reading is published. Most wind forecasts sit at 2-3 m/s whatever was observed; humidity forecasts stay near 75-90%; pressure forecasts follow higher pressures but stay too high on low-pressure days; rainfall forecasts sit at 1-5 mm almost regardless of the observed amount (too wet on dry days, too dry on wet days).
